question: Which of the following best describes synchronous interactions in tele-nursing?

options.B: Real-time video consultations and phone calls
options.C: Transmitting delayed data via secure messaging
options.D: Filing paper health records in a clinic

explanation: Synchronous interactions refer to real-time communication methods between the nurse and patient, such as video calls and telephone conversations. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is a primary benefit of integrating tele-nursing into healthcare delivery systems?

options.A: Eliminating the need for physical hospitals entirely
options.B: Extending care reach to underserved rural populations
options.C: Increasing the physical workload of bedside nurses
options.D: Replacing physicians with autonomous nursing robots

explanation: Tele-nursing allows nurses to overcome geographical barriers and provide essential health services to remote and underserved populations. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which tele-nursing model involves transmitting clinical photographs and test results for later evaluation?
explanation: Store-and-forward technology allows clinical data and media to be transmitted securely for review by a healthcare provider at a later time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why are mobile health (mHealth) models particularly effective in many developing settings?

options.B: They rely on widespread mobile network infrastructure
options.C: They eliminate the need for any nursing documentation
options.D: They replace all medications with digital apps

explanation: mHealth leverages the widespread availability of mobile phones and cellular networks to deliver health services effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following is considered a specialized peripheral device used in tele-nursing?
explanation: Digital stethoscopes and other Bluetooth-enabled devices are specialized peripherals used to capture and transmit patient data during virtual assessments. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is a major infrastructure challenge often encountered in tele-nursing within resource-limited settings?

options.A: An excess of high-speed fiber-optic cables
options.B: Erratic power supply and limited internet bandwidth
options.C: Too many software updates per day
options.D: Absence of any mobile phones in the population

explanation: Unreliable electricity and limited internet bandwidth are common technical barriers affecting virtual healthcare delivery in resource-limited regions. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which organization is primarily responsible for regulating professional nursing practice in Nigeria?

options.B: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating nursing education and practice standards in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why is data privacy compliance crucial in tele-nursing?

options.A: To prevent unauthorized access to sensitive patient health records
options.B: To increase the speed of internet downloads
options.C: To eliminate the need for patient documentation
options.D: To reduce the cost of mobile data subscriptions

explanation: Adhering to data protection regulations safeguards confidential patient information from cyber threats and unauthorized disclosure. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is a primary communication requirement for nurses conducting virtual patient assessments?

options.A: Using complex medical jargon to show expertise
options.B: Speaking quickly to save consultation time
options.C: Using clear, concise language free of medical jargon
options.D: Avoiding eye contact entirely through the camera

explanation: Clear and simple communication ensures that patients and caregivers easily understand health instructions provided during virtual sessions. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h5)

question: In the absence of physical touch during a tele-nursing consultation, what must nurses rely on heavily?

options.A: Active listening, visual observation, and structured questioning
options.B: Guessing the patient's diagnosis without asking questions
options.D: Relying solely on automated computer diagnostics

explanation: Virtual nurses must sharpen their observational skills and use structured questions and active listening to assess patients accurately. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of tele-nursing in chronic disease management?

options.A: Increasing the frequency of emergency room admissions
options.B: Providing continuous monitoring and tracking of medication adherence
options.C: Replacing all prescription medications with herbal remedies
options.D: Discouraging patients from managing their own health

explanation: Tele-nursing facilitates continuous monitoring and supports medication adherence to prevent chronic disease complications. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h6)

question: How do remote patient monitoring tools assist nurses managing patients with heart failure?

options.A: By tracking weight fluctuations and early signs of fluid overload
options.B: By performing major surgical procedures remotely
options.C: By dispensing physical intravenous medications automatically
options.D: By eliminating the need for any clinical documentation

explanation: Monitoring daily weight and vital signs helps nurses detect early fluid retention and prevent acute heart failure exacerbations. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is a practical solution for tele-nursing in communities with erratic electricity supply?

options.B: Using solar-powered charging stations for mobile devices
options.C: Relying exclusively on desktop computers requiring high power
options.D: Demanding patients travel to urban centers daily

explanation: Solar-powered charging stations provide a reliable energy source for mobile devices used in off-grid and resource-limited communities. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h7)

question: How can nursing professionals address digital illiteracy among elderly patients?

options.A: Refusing to provide care to anyone who cannot use a smartphone
options.B: Conducting community health education and teaching basic digital skills
options.C: Requiring family members to make all medical decisions
options.D: Using complex applications without patient involvement

explanation: Community health education and guided training help bridge the digital literacy gap for patients unfamiliar with technology. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is a major expected future trend in tele-nursing technology?

options.A: Complete abandonment of electronic health records
options.B: Integration of artificial intelligence and wearable biosensors
options.C: Exclusive reliance on paper-based documentation systems
options.D: Elimination of the need for nursing professionals

explanation: Future tele-nursing trends heavily feature AI analytics and wearable biosensors for advanced real-time health tracking. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h8)

question: Why must nursing education curricula incorporate health informatics and digital literacy?

options.A: To prepare nurses to function effectively as digital health coordinators
options.B: To ensure nurses spend zero time interacting with patients
options.C: To replace all clinical bedside skills with computer programming
options.D: To comply with hardware manufacturing sales quotas

explanation: Modern nurses need digital competencies to manage telehealth technologies and coordinate virtual care safely and efficiently. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h8)
